summary: A philosopher and religious studies scholar, Nae Ionescu studied at the University of Bucharest (~1908–1912), the University of Göttingen (~1913–1914), and the University of Munich (~1915–1919). He held a post at the University of Bucharest (~1920–1938).
Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Nagin J. Shah succeeded Dalsukh D. Malvania and served as Acting Director at the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (attested 1968).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Nalinaksha Dutt studied at Chittagong College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta (PhD), and SOAS University of London (DLitt). He held posts at Judson College, University of Calcutta, The Asiatic Society, and Maha Bodhi Society.

An Indologist and linguist, Nalini Balbir studied under Colette Caillat. She held research and academic posts at the CNRS (1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (from 1988), INALCO (~1988), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2000).

A scholar of religious studies and Indology, Nalini Devdas earned her PhD at Concordia University under Leslie Orr, having also studied under Steven Collins and others. She was affiliated with Carleton University (attested 2004).

A scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and history, Nam-lin Hur studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University (PhD) under Helen Hardacre. He held posts at Harvard University and the University of British Columbia.

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Naman P. Ahuja earned a doctorate from SOAS University of London. He was appointed Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Namgyal Rinpoche studied at the University of Michigan, Jarvis Baptist Seminary, and under teachers including Sayadaw U Thila Wunta and the 16th Karmapa. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1965) and the Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Namio Egami studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1967) and directed the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Specializing in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Namita Das completed a PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Namkhai Norbu studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and Khams bre bshad grwa. He held posts at Southwest Minzu University, IsMEO, and the University of Naples from the 1960s to 1992.

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Nancy Hock earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (1987) under Joanna Gottfried Williams. She held a post at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (attested 1987).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Nancy Lin pursued graduate studies at Columbia University and earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, studying under teachers including Bryan J. Cuevas and Michael Hahn.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, Nancy McCagney studied under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa and Ninian Smart. She held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, Nani Gopal Majumdar studied at the University of Calcutta (~1916–1920). He served as Superintendent at the Indian Museum (~1929–1938) and the Archaeological Survey of India (1931).

A specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Naoji Okuyama completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985). He held teaching posts at Tohoku University (~1985–1993) and became a professor at Koyasan University (~1993).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Naoki Nabeshima served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University, where he also founded the Open Research Center for Humanities, Science and Religion (attested 2004).
Specializing in Indology, Naoko Nishimura completed a PhD at Tohoku University (by 2002) under Toshifumi Goto and later served as a researcher there (attested 2012).
